## Overview

In this first Final Project checkpoint,
you will submit a summary of what you plan to do for your Final Project.
We're calling this a "proposal", because we'll discuss it with each of you in brief
meetings the week after the deadline, to give you some feedback and guidance
before you start working on the project in earnest.

We're quite flexible about what your project will be,
so we expect that for most of you, whatever topic you pick will be acceptable.
However, if you are really unsure about your project idea,
it's a good idea to check with us _before you start working on this proposal_.

## Directions and grading

### Submission expectations

- **Deadline**: [Sunday Nov 15^th^ at 11:59 pm]{style="background-color: #faf678;"}.
- **Submission**: Submit your assignment by tagging `@kstarr791` and `@jelmerp`
  in an Issue in your GitHub repo.

### Rubric

You can earn a total of 10 points:
2 points for each of the 5 main steps below (items 3–7). [POINT FOR ORAL DISCUSSION?]
For each items, for full points,
we'd like to see some level of detail and thoughtfulness in your answers.
It doesn't matter if you're still uncertain about many aspects of your project,
but it should be clear that you have thought seriously about the project.

And while you're allowed to use genAI tools to help you with your proposal,
we expect (though will not directly enforce) that the proposal is largely written by yourself.
In the oral discussion with us,
we will make sure that you understand what you've written down,
and if not, points may be deducted.

## Detailed steps

### Setting up

1. Create a directory `/fs/ess/PAS3493/people/$USER/FP` for your project,
   and initialize a Git repository there.

   _This will be a directory and repository that you will continue throughout the_
   _Final Project, and won't just be for this proposal._

2. Write your proposal in a file `doc/proposal.md`.

### The proposal

3. Start with a general description of what your project will be about.
   Describe what data you will work with and what kind of output your project will produce.

4. Summarize how you envision the more technical aspects:
   for example, you can mention how you will structure and run your scripts,
   which programs you plan to use, or which kinds of analyses you plan to perform,
   and how you will structure your results.

5. Check the list of graded aspects on the
   [page with general information about the project](./FP-info.qmd).
   You may also already refer to the more detailed
   [grading rubric on the page about you project's final submission](./FP4.qmd#rubric).
   If you are not sure you will be able to fulfill one of these aspects,
   or intend to skip something, mention that in your proposal.

6. Describe which aspects of your project you are still uncertain about,
   for instance because you intend to include some topics that we have yet to cover
   in the course, or because you're not sure how far you will get.

7. Describe why you chose to pick this project.
   For example, because it will be useful for your research, or because it gives
   you practice with coding topics that you want to improve on.

### Submitting your proposal

8. Create a new, empty, public repository for your project on GitHub,
   push your local repo to GitHub,
   and tag Kelsey (`@kstarr791`) and Jelmer (`@jelmerp`) in a GitHub "Issue" for
   your repo.
